title: Ala. Code § 6-2-38 — Limitations on personal actions
content:
Ala. Code § 6-2-38

Within two years: Actions for any injury to the person or rights of another, not arising from contract and not hereinafter enumerated.

title: Alaska Stat. § 09.10.070 — Personal injury and wrongful death
content:
Alaska Stat. § 09.10.070

(a) An action for the recovery of a fine or penalty, or for damages for an injury to the person or property, or for trespass for injury to real property, or for waste, or for libel, slander, or false imprisonment, or for seduction, or for criminal conversation, or for breach of promise of marriage, or for deceit or fraud, shall be commenced within two years.

title: Ark. Code Ann. § 16-56-105 — Personal injury actions
content:
Ark. Code Ann. § 16-56-105

(a)(1) All actions for any injury to the person or rights of another, not arising on contract and not hereinafter enumerated, shall be commenced within three (3) years after the cause of action accrues.

title: Haw. Rev. Stat. § 657-7 — Personal injuries; libel and slander
content:
Haw. Rev. Stat. § 657-7

Actions for the recovery of any penalty or forfeiture, or for damages for an injury to the person or reputation, or for libel, slander, or false imprisonment, or for seduction, or for criminal conversation, or for breach of promise of marriage, or for deceit or fraud, shall be commenced within two years after the cause of action accrued.

title: Idaho Code § 5-219 — Actions for personal injury
content:
Idaho Code § 5-219

Actions for assault, battery, or false imprisonment, or for any other injury to the person or rights of another not arising on contract and not hereinafter enumerated, shall be commenced within two years.

title: Ind. Code § 34-11-2-4 — Actions for personal injuries
content:
Ind. Code § 34-11-2-4

An action for injuries to the person or for wrongful death must be commenced within two (2) years after the cause of action accrues.

title: Iowa Code § 614.1 — Personal injury
content:
Iowa Code § 614.1

2. The following actions may be brought at any time within two years after the cause of action accrues: ... b. An action for any other injury to the person or reputation of another.

title: Kan. Stat. Ann. § 60-513 — Personal actions
content:
Kan. Stat. Ann. § 60-513

(a) An action for any of the following causes shall be brought within two years: (1) Recovery of damages suffered as a result of injury to the person or injury to the rights of another not arising on contract.

title: Ky. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 413.140 — Actions to be brought within one year
content:
Ky. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 413.140

(1)(a) The following actions shall be commenced within one (1) year after the cause of action accrued: ... 4. An action for an injury to the person of another not resulting in death.

title: La. Civ. Code art. 3492 — Delictual actions
content:
La. Civ. Code art. 3492

Delictual actions are subject to a liberative prescription of one year. This prescription commences to run from the day injury or damage is sustained.

title: Me. Rev. Stat. tit. 14, § 752 — Personal actions
content:
Me. Rev. Stat. tit. 14, § 752

All civil actions for assault and battery, false imprisonment, libel, slander, malicious prosecution, criminal conversation, seduction, breach of promise of marriage, or for any other injury to the person or reputation, or for any other injury to the person or rights of another not arising on contract and not hereinafter enumerated, shall be commenced within 6 years after the cause of action accrues.

title: Minn. Stat. § 541.07 — Two-year limitation
content:
Minn. Stat. § 541.07

The following actions shall be commenced within two years: (1) for libel, slander, assault, battery, false imprisonment, or other tort resulting in personal injury, and all actions against veterinarians for malpractice or negligence.

title: Miss. Code Ann. § 15-1-49 — Personal injury
content:
Miss. Code Ann. § 15-1-49

(1) All actions for which no other period of limitation is prescribed shall be commenced within three (3) years next after the cause of such action accrued, and not after.

title: Mo. Rev. Stat. § 516.120 — Personal actions
content:
Mo. Rev. Stat. § 516.120

Except as otherwise provided in this section, actions for any injury to the person or rights of another, not arising on contract and not hereinafter enumerated, shall be brought within five years.

title: Mont. Code Ann. § 27-2-204 — Injury to person or property
content:
Mont. Code Ann. § 27-2-204

(1) Within 3 years: An action for assault, battery, false imprisonment, or for any other injury to the person or rights of another not arising on contract and not hereinafter enumerated.

title: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-207 — Personal injury actions
content:
Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-207

An action for any injury to the person or rights of another, not arising on contract and not hereinafter enumerated, can only be commenced within four years.

title: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 11.190 — Limitations for personal injury
content:
Nev. Rev. Stat. § 11.190

4. Within 2 years: An action to recover damages for injuries to a person or for injuring the rights of another not arising on contract.

title: N.H. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 508:4 — Personal actions
content:
N.H. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 508:4

Personal Actions. All personal actions, except actions for slander or libel, may be brought only within 3 years of the time the cause of action accrued.

title: N.M. Stat. Ann. § 37-1-8 — Personal injury actions
content:
N.M. Stat. Ann. § 37-1-8

Except as otherwise provided in the New Mexico Statutes Annotated, actions for any injury to the person, property or reputation of another not arising on contract and not hereinafter enumerated shall be brought within three years.

title: N.D. Cent. Code § 28-01-16 — Personal injury actions
content:
N.D. Cent. Code § 28-01-16

Except as otherwise provided by law, an action for relief on the ground of fraud, an action for trespass upon real property, an action for taking, detaining, or injuring personal property, or for an injury to the person or rights of another not arising on contract, and not hereinafter enumerated, may not be commenced after six years.

title: Okla. Stat. tit. 12, § 95 — Limitations on personal actions
content:
Okla. Stat. tit. 12, § 95

C. Civil actions other than for the recovery of real property can only be brought within the following periods, after the cause of action accrues: ... 3. For injury to the person or rights of another, not arising on contract, and not hereinafter enumerated, within two (2) years.

title: Or. Rev. Stat. § 12.110 — Actions for certain injuries to person not arising on contract
content:
Or. Rev. Stat. § 12.110

(1) An action for assault, battery, false imprisonment, or for any other injury to the person or rights of another not arising on contract and not hereinafter enumerated, shall be commenced within two years.

title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-1-14 — Personal actions
content:
R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-1-14

Actions for injuries to the person shall be commenced and sued within three (3) years next after the cause of action shall accrue, and not after.

title: S.C. Code Ann. § 15-3-530 — Three years
content:
S.C. Code Ann. § 15-3-530

Within three years: (1) an action for the recovery of damages for injury to the person or for injury to the rights of another not arising on contract.

title: S.D. Codified Laws § 15-2-15 — Personal injury actions
content:
S.D. Codified Laws § 15-2-15

An action for any injury to the person or rights of another not arising on contract and not hereinafter enumerated shall be commenced within three years.

title: Tenn. Code Ann. § 28-3-104 — Personal actions
content:
Tenn. Code Ann. § 28-3-104

(a) The following actions shall be commenced within one (1) year after the cause of action accrued: (1) Actions for injuries to the person or character of another.

title: Utah Code § 78B-2-307 — Personal injury actions
content:
Utah Code § 78B-2-307

An action may be brought within four years for any injury to the person or rights of another not arising on contract and not otherwise enumerated.

title: Vt. Stat. Ann. tit. 12, § 512 — Personal actions
content:
Vt. Stat. Ann. tit. 12, § 512

Actions for assault and battery, libel and slander, shall be commenced within three years and actions for personal injury caused by negligence shall be commenced within three years after the cause of action accrues.

title: W. Va. Code § 55-2-12 — Personal actions
content:
W. Va. Code § 55-2-12

Every action to recover damages for an injury to the person, or for an injury when the person is in custody, or for wrongful death, or for injury to personal or real property, shall be brought within two years next after the cause of action accrued.

title: Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 1-3-105 — Personal injury actions
content:
Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 1-3-105

Every action for an injury to the person, or for an injury when the person is in custody, or for wrongful death, or for injury to personal or real property, shall be brought within four (4) years.

title: D.C. Code § 12-301 — Limitations on personal actions
content:
D.C. Code § 12-301

(3) for the recovery of damages for an injury or disease to personal property or to real property, or for a personal injury or disease, or for libel or slander, or for malicious prosecution, or for false arrest or false imprisonment, or for the recovery of a chattel, or for a statutory penalty, or for a breach of contract or express or implied warranty, or for an account receivable, or for a judgment, or for any other cause of action not specified in this section, or for which a period of limitation is not specially prescribed by law, within three years.
